2x=4002x = 4002x=400

x=200x = 200x=200

Sunil's share = 4x=4×200=Rs 8004x = 4 \times 200 = \text{Rs } 8004x=4×200=Rs 800

From the given totals, we can write:

Total with M = (M and P only) + (M and C only) + (all three)

23 = x + y + 18

Therefore: x+y=5x + y = 5x+y=5

For Physics (P):

Total with P = (M and P only) + (P and C only) + (all three)

25 = x + z + 18

Therefore: x+z=7x + z = 7x+z=7

From our equations:

x+y=5x + y = 5x+y=5 so y=5−xy = 5 - xy=5−x

x+z=7x + z = 7x+z=7 so z=7−xz = 7 - xz=7−x

For Chemistry (C):

Total with C = (M and C only) + (P and C only) + (all three)

Total with C = y+z+18y + z + 18y+z+18

Total with C = (5−x)+(7−x)+18(5 - x) + (7 - x) + 18(5−x)+(7−x)+18

Total with C = 30−2x30 - 2x30−2x

To minimize the number of students with Chemistry, we need to maximize x.

Constraints on x:

Since y=5−x≥0y = 5 - x \geq 0y=5−x≥0, we need x≤5x \leq 5x≤5

z=7−5=2z = 7 - 5 = 2z=7−5=2

Minimum students with Chemistry = 30−2(5)=2030 - 2(5) = 2030−2(5)=20

Therefore, the smallest possible number of students choosing Chemistry is 20.

questions.question_text: John takes twice as much time as Jack to finish a job. Jack and Jim together take one-thirds of the time to finish the job than John takes working alone. Second condition: Jack and Jim together take one-third the time John takes alone.

  • John alone takes 2J days
  • Jack and Jim together take 2J3\dfrac{2J}{3}32J​ days
  • Combined rate of Jack and Jim = 32J\dfrac{3}{2J}2J3​ jobs per day

Since Jack and Jim's combined rate = Jack's rate + Jim's rate:

32J=1J+Jim’s rate\dfrac{3}{2J} = \dfrac{1}{J} + \text{Jim's rate}2J3​=J1​+Jim’s rate

Jim’s rate=32J−1J=32J−22J=12J\text{Jim's rate} = \dfrac{3}{2J} - \dfrac{1}{J} = \dfrac{3}{2J} - \dfrac{2}{2J} = \dfrac{1}{2J}Jim’s rate=2J3​−J1​=2J3​−2J2​=2J1​

Therefore, Jim takes 2J days to finish the job alone.

All three working together:

  • Combined rate = 1J+12J+12J=1J+22J=1J+1J=2J\dfrac{1}{J} + \dfrac{1}{2J} + \dfrac{1}{2J} = \dfrac{1}{J} + \dfrac{2}{2J} = \dfrac{1}{J} + \dfrac{1}{J} = \dfrac{2}{J}J1​+2J1​+2J1​=J1​+2J2​=J1​+J1​=J2​
  • Time taken together = J2\dfrac{J}{2}2J​ days

The condition states: John takes 3 days more than all three working together.

2J=J2+32J = \dfrac{J}{2} + 32J=2J​+3

2J−J2=32J - \dfrac{J}{2} = 32J−2J​=3

4J−J2=3\dfrac{4J - J}{2} = 324J−J​=3

3J2=3\dfrac{3J}{2} = 323J​=3

J=2J = 2J=2

Since J = 2:

  • Jack takes 2 days
  • John takes 4 days
  • Jim takes 2J = 4 days

Therefore, Jim will finish the job in 4 days working alone.
